rv.q: His play is brilliantly fuelled by theatrical manners and by Shakespearean quotes and references.

We follow the company, principally in Sir’s dressing room but also in the wings thanks to Michael Taylor’s wonderful manually revolving set, through a day that sees his 277th performance as King Lear, a fatalistic mental crisis and . . . well, if you don’t already know the ending, you can surely guess.
It's a real pity, then, that Sean Foley's somewhat lacklustre production doesn't make a convincing case for a West End revival in 2016.
Sean Foley's production of The Dresser is simply extraordinary.
The Dresser is a wonderful depiction of actors and their business that is funny and moving at different points and occasionally simultaneously.
Sean Foley's new staging is blessed with two utterly tremendous performances that make the sense of hopelessness and hope that they respectively embody to shine through.
Overall, an intriguing and compelling production.

Back in 1983 I had the extraordinary privilege of witnessing Albert Finney and Tom Courtenay deliver two of the most theatrically ebullient performances about the grandeur and grimness of a life in luvvydom, ever committed to celluloid.
Ken Stott in the wan London revival of Ronald Harwood's 1980 play 'The Dresser' is offering little in the way of competition.
Sir Ronald Harwood's 'behind-the-scenes' vivid exploration of the duality of performance is given a gripping and heart-rending revival.
Reece Shearsmith as the devoted dresser is giving the best performance I have seen him give: camp, waspish, sad, lonely, bitter, and finally deeply moving.
This is one show that deserves to go on.
In fact, the final 15 minutes of the play are some of the most well-acted and emotionally thrilling in the West End today.

cn.t: Harwood's backstage tragi-comedy endures with strong performances from Shearsmith and Stott, though this revival of the wartime theatrical tale receives mixed notices—praised for its sharp poignancy but questioned whether it still resonates after 36 years.
